data.short_description: Tinto, a Spanish-rooted wine, cocktail, sake and tapas bar, is planning to open on East 11th Street in Austin. Chef Daniel Boulud is bringing a new brasserie, Brasserie Boulud, to Manhattan at 1900 Broadway. The restaurant will feature favorites from Bar Boulud and Boulud Sud alongside new signature dishes. No official opening date has been announced yet.

Culture, a Greek yogurt shop founded by Jenny and Gino Ammirati, is opening its third location at 205 Third Ave. in Manhattan's Gramercy neighborhood. The new spot will serve the same yogurt as its Park Slope and West Village locations but with more frozen yogurt machines and flavors. It marks the brand's 15th anniversary.

Westy's, a 42-year Pinch District staple, served its final dinner on August 15 and announced its closure on Facebook. Owner Jake Schorr cited declining sales, increasing debt, and inflation, according to WREG. The building and synagogue remain for sale, and Schorr is also recovering from a medical procedure.

Sirincci Coffee Company, which has two Slidell locations, is adding a third location in Lacombe, taking over the former White House Coffee and Creamery. The transition begins in mid-August, with owners pledging to honor the previous business while introducing their own brand. The Lacombe shop will likely carry the brand's signature espresso and food menu.

The opening lineup includes gift boxes, preserves, strawberry yuzu lemonade, and pastries made with chef Yoshie Nakanishi and Lady M.

1972 Women's Sports Pub, Texas' first bar dedicated to women's and gender-expansive sports, will permanently close its Guadalupe St. location on August 30. The closure is tied to the property being acquired through eminent domain for the Project Connect transit project. Owners have no immediate relocation plans.

Paul Revere Restaurant, a 26-year West Medford breakfast and lunch destination, will serve its final dinner on August 30. The owner's serious medical hardship prompted retirement and the decision to close. The restaurant was known for its cozy atmosphere and American comfort food.
